notes: TBox rule edit, on the same class as technology-replace-0005 but a different rule. No real exceptions among Unix-like systems: POSIX ends a line with the newline character (on EBCDIC z/OS UNIX System Services it is the EBCDIC newline, the same character in another code page; noted as the one edge case considered). CRLF is plausible (it is Windows' convention) and clearly false. The well-known member is Linux (verifier change; the writer had macOS): macOS's LF is rarely stated by name in Dolma ('macOS uses LF' 3, 'Mac OS X uses LF' 2) and competes with the classic-Mac 'Mac uses CR' (20) and 'Macs use CR' (15), so a by-name world for it was weak, and leaving the class would also fight its UNIX 03 certification; 'Linux uses LF' has 44 exact hits. Linux is also 0005's well-known member, for a different rule; the membership prompt is worded differently. The near query asks classic Mac OS (CR), whose answer differs from the new one; Windows was avoided because its CRLF equals the new answer.
